seed_situation: Your younger sister works as a receptionist at a community dental practice. She tells you privately that she initialed the end-of-day room-cleaning checklist for one treatment room without actually checking it, because she was rushing to leave; no patient was affected, and the room was cleaned later by another staff member. The checklist is only used for internal routine checks, and no current patient is at risk. She asks you not to mention it to the office manager, saying it is only a paperwork slip and she is afraid of being written up during her probation period. You feel caught between not wanting her punished over a small lapse and not wanting a false entry to become normal in a place that depends on accurate routines.
why_it_is_hard: The tension is between protecting a sibling from a consequence that may be disproportionate and refusing to treat a false workplace record as harmless. If you stay close and silent, you may preserve her trust but allow a standard to slip; if you push for correction, you may protect the practice's integrity but cost her job security and strain the family bond.
varied_fact: the outcome is a minor administrative lapse with no patient impact rather than a falsified safety record tied to a patient infection

situation_features.note: the asker has no formal role in the practice and learns of the lapse privately

seed_situation: Your younger sister works as a receptionist at a community dental practice. She tells you privately that she initialed the sterilization safety log for a set of instruments without actually confirming they had been processed; the instruments were later used on one patient who developed an infection. The set has already been removed from use and no current patient is at immediate risk, but the false entry remains in the record. She asks you not to mention what she told you, saying she did not mean to hurt anyone and is afraid of losing her job. You feel caught between keeping her confidence and knowing that a false safety record is now tied to a patient's harm.
why_it_is_hard: The tension is between loyalty to a frightened sibling and accountability for a false record connected to patient harm. Keeping her confidence may preserve family trust but leave patients, staff, and the practice unprotected; pressing disclosure may protect others but impose a heavy cost on her and on the relationship.
varied_fact: the outcome is a falsified safety record tied to a patient infection rather than a minor administrative lapse with no patient impact

situation_features.note: the asker has no formal role in the practice and learns of the falsification privately

seed_situation: You are a staff nurse on a district nursing team with no supervisory role. During a private home visit, a senior healthcare assistant stayed an extra forty minutes with a recently bereaved patient while you waited because the next visit needed two staff; the following dressing started twenty minutes late and the patient was mildly distressed. You have already decided that the assistant's over-involvement caused the delay, and you want permission to ask the team coordinator to correct her before Friday's roster meeting.
why_it_is_hard: The difficulty is whether your immediate disapproval is a usable perception of a real lapse or a self-protective reflex that should be examined and possibly corrected; acting on it may burden a colleague and discourage attentive care to a lonely patient, while setting it aside may leave a genuine pattern of delay unexamined.

situation_features.relationship: colleagues on the same district nursing team; the person you want corrected is a senior healthcare assistant, not your manager
situation_features.note: the asker has already decided and is seeking permission; the matter is private and only time-sensitive because of an upcoming roster meeting

seed_situation: You work part-time as a learning support mentor at a further education college and have no authority over the hardship panel, but students come to you for help writing applications. Only two applicants can get your intensive one-to-one support before the panel meets next month, and your sister has privately asked you to make sure her lodger, a care leaver who may lose his room, gets one of those places. Another student with a similar housing risk has already booked the second place, and you are torn between helping the lodger and keeping your support available on the same terms to everyone.
why_it_is_hard: A personal claim through your sister pulls you to use your inside knowledge to protect someone from serious loss, while your college role exists to give applicants the same access to help; giving him extra support may prevent homelessness for him but quietly disadvantage another needy student, and refusing may leave a close family claim unanswered.

situation_features.relationship: the applicant is your sister's lodger; you also have a professional support relationship with another student applicant
situation_features.note: the college role gives insider knowledge and influence but no formal decision power over the fund

seed_situation: During an evening shift at an ambulance dispatch centre, a newly qualified call-taker logs a minor fall at a care home as needing prompt assessment, and a senior dispatcher beside them changes it to a routine transport while saying within earshot of the floor, 'We don't send urgent crews for wobbly ankles.' The care home resident is not in danger, but the call-taker believes the wording misrepresents the assessment and will make the care home stop reporting small incidents. The crew assignment is due at the next handover in five minutes, and the call-taker wants the senior's change challenged in front of the team so everyone sees they were wrong.
why_it_is_hard: The senior has practical standing and the dispatch queue cannot pause, while the call-taker's objection is about accuracy and respect rather than immediate patient danger. Pushing back publicly could humiliate the senior and disrupt the shift, but letting it pass could distort the record and teach the call-taker that experience overrides honest judgment.

situation_features.relationship: newly qualified call-taker and senior dispatcher acting as informal lead
situation_features.note: semi-public dispatch floor, immediate handover, minor patient impact, asker wants to prevail

seed_situation: I work as a pharmacy technician in a hospital pharmacy, with no supervisory role. My sister is a nurse on a busy ward, and a few times a week she asks me at the open dispensing counter, where other technicians can hear, to move her routine medication top-ups ahead of the queue. I have been doing it because she is family and because saying no in front of her colleagues feels harsh, so I tell myself it is only a few minutes and no patient is hurt. Other wards now wait a little longer, and one coworker joked that some people get a fast lane, but nobody has raised it formally.
why_it_is_hard: A real family claim and the wish to avoid a public scene press against the fairness owed to other wards and coworkers, and keeping quiet preserves peace only by hiding the objection. Speaking plainly risks embarrassing the sister and stirring conflict, while saying nothing lets an unfair habit continue.

situation_features.relationship: adult siblings, one a pharmacy technician and one a ward nurse
situation_features.note: The requester has no formal authority over the queue, but can influence the order of routine tasks; the partiality is visible to coworkers and affects other wards only slightly.

seed_situation: Your mother lives in a residential dementia unit, and you use a small personal allowance to pay for two extra evening companions for her each week. At an open family-council meeting, another resident's daughter asks whether you would give up one of those visits for the next few nights because her father is becoming unsettled after dark and the unit has no spare volunteers. Before you can answer, your mother says loudly that your money is for her alone and that the other family should manage their own problems. The other daughter is hurt, the coordinator suggests a conversation tomorrow, and you want a practical wording that protects your budget, stops the feud, and tells you whether and how to correct your mother's remark.
why_it_is_hard: The pull is between your mother's stronger claim on your limited help and a stranger's real, time-sensitive need, while any correction of your mother risks humiliating her or straining the bond, and silence may endorse a refusal you doubt is right. Neither letting the family claim override the outsider nor flattening the two claims into equal ones removes the cost; the conflict is about who should bear the burden of your scarce resource and how far a child may press a parent.

situation_features.relationship: adult child and parent; another resident's adult child is a stranger with a competing claim
situation_features.note: Public disagreement in a care setting; touches the unresolved question of how far correction inside the parent-child bond should go.

seed_situation: I am a trainee at a fertility clinic, learning to run the required medication-safety teaching session in front of a small group. Partway through my supervised practice, one patient says they are shaking and nauseous because they fasted for bloodwork, and they need to eat something in the next few minutes. My assessment checklist requires me to complete the full script and sign-off without breaking the sequence, and my supervisor is watching while the other patients wait. I feel torn between finishing the form correctly and letting them step out immediately.
why_it_is_hard: Keeping to the sequence protects the meaning of the training form and the discipline the trainee is supposed to be learning, while breaking it responds to a visible, immediate need. The patient bears the cost of continued nausea if the form is kept, and the trainee and clinic bear the cost of a disrupted record and a weakened lesson if it is broken.

situation_features.relationship: trainee and patient during a supervised group teaching session
situation_features.note: The asker has no authority and is being assessed on following a formal procedure; the need is minor, immediate, and publicly visible.
